body:
Neovim>=0.13 is planned to have multicursor functionality (neovim/neovim#41587), which introduces a visible amount of issues with 'mini.nvim' compatibility. This issue is meant to track them until they are resolved.

Most likely to be an upstream issue (without a known/possible way to fix this in 'mini.nvim'):

- 'mini.cursorword' and 'mini.trailspace' highlighting is drawn on top of multicursor highlighting. See neovim/neovim#41629.

- Most (if not any) movement mappings won't currently work with `zq`, since it doesn't support "textobjects, Lua, `<Cmd>` or ":" mappings" (`:h zq`). This affects 'mini.jump' (overrides `f`, `t`, `F`, `T`), `n` / `N` overrides, etc.

Solved:
- ~~'mini.clue' overrides a `Q` mapping to correctly replay the latest recording. This mirrors the built-in `Q`, but that has been repurposed for multicursor. The best solution is still merging upstream neovim/neovim#24565, but in the meantime not overriding `Q` is good enough.~~ This should be solved on latest `main` by just not creating both `@` and `Q` custom mappings altogether. It *seems* that everything works without them present 🤞
- ~~'mini.basics' overrides built-in `<C-l>` mapping ("clear" action, including now multicursors) for a window navigation. I still think that it is better suited for window navigation, so probably creating something like `<Esc>` to serve as "clear" is reasonable.~~ This should be solved on latest `main` by 'mini.basics' creating a `<C-c>` basic mapping for "Stop, clear, redraw".
- ~~Visually selecting 'mini.ai' textobjects only selects the main cursor and not extra cursors.~~ Should be (mostly) resolved on the latest `main`. There are some odd misplacing of the edit only once, but that doesn't look like a 'mini.ai' issue.
- ~~'mini.bracketed': custom mappings for `u` and `<C-r>` affect how undo/redo is done when multicursor follow mode is enabled. See neovim/neovim#42037.~~
- ~~'mini.move': moving Visual selection. See neovim/neovim#42005~~. Should be resolved on latest Neovim `master`.
- ~~Most parts of 'mini.surround' and `?` textobject in 'mini.ai' don't fully work during multicursor editing. The reason is very technical and comes down to how their operators/textobjects interact with the new `CmdAtom` event. See neovim/neovim#41657.~~ Should be resolved on latest `main`.
- ~~The `exchange` operator in 'mini.operators' doesn't cascade because 1) first step doesn't trigger cascade (it is not text edit or cursor move); 2) requires manual tracking of regions per cursor *and* info about how to match them between steps.~~ Should be resolved on latest `main`: 1) hack force cascade on first step by doing dummy text edit; 2) track regions per cursor (rely on `vim.v.cascading` to smartly decide which step it is) and rely on them being cascaded in "reasonably same" order. As extra cursors are implemented as extmarks (which update per id and not create new ones), the order at first and second steps seems to _be preserved.

    Ideally, more public API would help here. Like 1) dedicated way to force cascade (see neovim/neovim#42279); 2) more info and/or guarantees about cascade (notion of "extra cursor id" and which one is current during cascade; order guarantees). For now, let's hope it will keep working in at least common and simple situations like `gxiw` - `w` - `.`.

- ~~'mini.bracketed' overrides `[C` and `]C` multicursor navigation mappings (those are first/last comment). I don't like the idea of changing the suffix for `comment` target (breaking change). Instead adding a dedicated target for multicursor might be an option.~~ There is now `multicursor` target with default `m` suffix. It has several improvements over built-ins: `first` and `last` direction, extra cursor rotation in follow mode.


---

This is meant as a tracking issue for maintainers and public. For an unintended behavior that is not listed here, please create a separate issue (which can be discussed there and then listed here).

comment_data.body:
> 'mini.basics' overrides built-in <C-l> mapping ("clear" action, including now multicursors) for a window navigation. I still think that it is better suited for window navigation, so probably creating something like <Esc> to serve as "clear" is reasonable.

I think that remapping `CTRL-W_L` to `CTRL-L` is an unofficial best practice, especially when working with splits is an important part of the users workflow.

> 'mini.bracketed' overrides [C and ]C multicursor navigation mappings (those are first/last comment). I don't like the idea of changing the suffix for comment target (breaking change). Instead adding a dedicated target for multicursor might be an option.

I'd argue that in this case the inconvenience of introducing a new mnemonic for builtin [C and ]C outweighs its current 'comment' usefulness. Perhaps in general, the 'first' and 'last' mappings for brackets that only act inside a single buffer seem less useful, as the movement can also be achieved by a combination of 'g/GG' and 'backward/forward'. I can't imagine that users often need to express an operation involving the first/last comment.
When using multicursors, [C and ]C have the potential to be used quite often.

Mini.bracketed does not create first and last mappings when the [suffix](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/9d01f392b33fb2ba36fbc87fc0bf4453e63ffb0a/lua/mini/bracketed.lua#L174) is not a letter. Perhaps we can add [C and ]C to that exception, keeping only [c and ]c

> Perhaps in general, the 'first' and 'last' mappings for brackets that only act inside a single buffer seem less useful, as the movement can also be achieved by a combination of 'g/GG' and 'backward/forward'.

I use it quite often with `[D`, `[I`, and `[H` (although not 'mini.bracketed', but still) Having to do `G]h` gets a bit a bit annoying.

> Mini.bracketed does not create first and last mappings when the [suffix](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/9d01f392b33fb2ba36fbc87fc0bf4453e63ffb0a/lua/mini/bracketed.lua#L174) is not a letter. Perhaps we can add [C and ]C to that exception, keeping only [c and ]c

This is because there is no full-proof way of choosing the "shifted" variants of not a letter. I don't really like the idea of intentional exceptions.

The current plan is to add a `multicursor` target with default `r` suffix. The `m` target is better mnemonic, of course, but `:h ]m` is present and seems to useful. But that is not final, maybe overriding `]m` is fine since its `(for Java or similar structured language)` limitation is a bit too narrow, especially with presence of `treesitter` target and the future 'mini.hierarchy'. Separate target will also add features like "go to first/last cursor".

Hi there! also mini.move is impacted by multicursor. Easily reproducible with:
- add 2 cursors in visual in 2 different lines
- move text right or left

It mixes both selections.

> Hi there! also mini.move is impacted by multicursor. Easily reproducible with:
> 
>     * add 2 cursors in visual in 2 different lines
> 
>     * move text right or left
> 
> 
> It mixes both selections.

Thanks! Yeah, I doubt this will get fixed, I am afraid. For technical reasons. Will take a look.

> Thanks! Yeah, I doubt this will get fixed, I am afraid. For technical reasons.

I figured! Your plugins were actually too perfect 👍 mCursor had just messed everything up adding a lot of complexity to handle
Also mini.cursorword overwrites color of multicursors if hl group with bg color is used.

> Also mini.cursorword overwrites color of multicursors if hl group with bg color is used.

That is unfortunately not fixable on 'mini.cursorword' side (without full rewrite into a more complex approach): neovim/neovim#41629. Hopefully it will be fixed before Neovim 0.13 release. In the meantime, default underline highlighting of 'mini.cursorword' works better than custom background highlighting.
Are the textobjects in `mini.ai` a known issue? I can `di(` and delete text at multiple cursors, but if I `vi(`, only the primary cursor will select the text.

> Are the textobjects in `mini.ai` a known issue? I can `di(` and delete text at multiple cursors, but if I `vi(`, only the primary cursor will select the text.

It seems that repeating Visual selection from plugins in general is problematic with multicursor. This is probably similar to 'mini.move' issue. I'll take a look.

> It seems that repeating Visual selection from plugins in general is problematic with multicursor.

Is this about `gv`? I am working on that

> > It seems that repeating Visual selection from plugins in general is problematic with multicursor.
> 
> Is this about `gv`? I am working on that

Not only. Any visual selection doesn't seem to work (like "move cursor" - `normal! o` -  "move cursor" in Visual mode or `1v` in Normal mode). I am in the process of creating an issue right now.

**Edit**: @justinmk, neovim/neovim#41956
With the `gv` issue fixed, `vi(` still doesn't work correctly. Are there further hurdles?
I have more fixes incoming, LMK if you see improvements tomorrow

> With the `gv` issue fixed, `vi(` still doesn't work correctly. Are there further hurdles?

Yeah, there were "hurdles" on the 'mini.ai' side. Visual selection mappings are implemented as expression mappings (for technical reasons) that precompute the reference region (against which to compute the textobject region) and codify it directly in the `'<Cmd>lua MiniAi.select_textobject(..., ..., { ..., reference_region = "", ... })<CR>'` type of returned value. This made each extra cursor use the reference region at main cursor to compute its target textobject region.

The solution here is to not precompute reference region. The best (and fairly satisfactory) way here is to make a small breaking change to `find_textobject()` (use current selection as default reference region in the Visual mode) which allows `select_textobject()` to dynamically compute the correct reference region.

I have a temporary branch with the solution (and a drive-by fixes+refactors) that seems to work with multicursor. I'd take another look on the fresh head before merging.

> I have a temporary branch with the solution (and a drive-by fixes+refactors) that seems to work with multicursor. I'd take another look on the fresh head before merging.

Should now be fixed on the latest `main`. There are some potential one-time glitches with editing, but that looks like something related to multicursor issues with Visual mode and `c` operator.
Evgeni and Justin working hard! Doing `vi(` with `mini.ai` now repeats the visual selection at multiple cursors, resolving my earlier question.

Pushed an update to `main` that makes all 'mini.nvim' modules work as good with multicursor as I can currently see reasonably possible. Most of modules "just work", the intervention required: 'mini.surround', 'mini.ai' (only for `?` textobject), 'mini.operators' `exchange` operator, 'mini.files' (to "constrain" extra cursor in the same way as the main one; #2551).

There is also a plan to address 'mini.bracketed' overriding `[C` / `]C`, probably by adding a new `[M` / `[m` / `]m` / `]M` target specifically for multicursor jumps.

The 'mini.bracketed' now has `multicursor` target with `m` suffix. So like `[M` / `[m` / `]m` / `]M` move to first / previous / next / last extra cursor with possible cursor rotation in follow mode. Unfortunately, this overrides built-in "method" motions, but they look *somewhat* redundant to me in presence of tree-sitter and other navigation methods.

With this, there are no obvious issues in 'mini.nvim' with the upcoming multicursor. I'll wait until the official Neovim=0.13 release to make sure that it is still the case and then close this. It still contains the searchable info about what doesn't work due to upstream temporary problems. (@justinmk, as I can miss the upstream PR that makes `zq` work with Lua and `<Cmd>` RHS, would you mind please pinging me if/when it happens).
